classes.name: General elections of members of the House of Representatives
classes.finest_note: The Commission's election reports give votes by polling station for each constituency (2025 report Appendix II); its results table gives constituency totals for 1946-2015. Polling-station returns before 2015 are not online.
classes.note: First past the post in single-member constituencies (36 under Constitution s.70(1), 41 since 2007). Parliament lasts five years from its first sitting unless dissolved sooner (s.68(2)), and a general election follows within three months of every dissolution (s.69(1)). The bicameral Parliament dates from the 1961 constitution; the 1946-1956 elections were to the unicameral Legislative Council.

cadence.locator: Constitution s.68(2): "Parliament, unless sooner dissolved, shall continue for five years from the date of its first sitting after any dissolution, and shall then stand dissolved"; s.69(1) general election within three months after every dissolution

classes.name_en: West Indies Federation House of Representatives (Trinidad and Tobago seats)
classes.note: Trinidad and Tobago returned 10 of the 45 members of the federal House at the only federal general election, 25 March 1958; the Federation was dissolved on 31 May 1962. Neither the date nor the seat count is quoted from a fetched official source.
classes.disposition_reason: The Commission's results table and reports do not include the 1958 federal election, and no official publication of its constituency returns is online.

dates.note: The only federal general election; not quoted from a fetched official source.

classes.name: Referendums
classes.disposition_reason: Neither the Constitution nor any electoral law provides for a referendum: the Constitution is altered by Act of Parliament passed by special majorities of both Houses (s.54), and no national or Tobago referendum has been held.

classes.name: The Senate
classes.disposition_reason: The 31 Senators are appointed by the President: 16 on the advice of the Prime Minister, 6 on that of the Leader of the Opposition, and 9 in the President's own discretion (Constitution s.40); none is elected.

classes.name: Election of the President by the Electoral College
classes.disposition_reason: The President is elected by secret ballot of the Electoral College, all members of the Senate and the House sitting together (Constitution ss.28-29), not by the public; the Prime Minister is appointed by the President from the House.

classes.name: Judges
classes.disposition_reason: The Chief Justice is appointed by the President after consultation with the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, and other judges on the advice of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission (Constitution ss.102 and 104); none is elected.

classes.name: Party candidate selections and internal elections
classes.disposition_reason: Parties screen and select candidates and elect their officers under their own rules; the Commission neither runs nor publishes these, and candidates enter the official process only on nomination day under the Representation of the People Act.

classes.name: Elections of Assemblymen to the Tobago House of Assembly
classes.finest_note: The Commission's THA reports give votes by polling station in each electoral district (2026 report Appendix II; reports for January and December 2021 are also posted). Reports for 1980-2017 are not online; the 2026 report's Appendix IX gives only island totals for them.
classes.note: First past the post in single-member electoral districts (12 until 2021, 15 since December 2021) under the Representation of the People Act (THA Act s.5(1)(a)). The Assembly lasts four years from its first sitting unless it dissolves itself sooner (s.22). Four appointed Councillors and the Presiding Officer complete the Assembly.

cadence.locator: THA Act s.22(1): "The Assembly shall continue for four years from the date of its first sitting after any primary election, and shall then stand dissolved, unless the Assembly, by resolution, dissolves"
cadence.administered_by: Elections and Boundaries Commission, through returning officers it appoints for each electoral district

classes.name: Bye-elections of Assemblymen to the Tobago House of Assembly
classes.note: A vacant Assemblyman's seat is filled at a bye-election, except near the end of the Assembly's term (THA Act s.21). No list of THA bye-elections has been reached.

cadence.administered_by: Elections and Boundaries Commission, through returning officers it appoints for each electoral district
cadence.vacancy_rule: The President, after consultation with the Prime Minister and the Chief Secretary, fixes a bye-election two to three months after the vacancy is declared; none is held within three months of a general THA election, and the President may decline one in the Assembly's last year (THA Act s.21).

classes.name: Chief Secretary, Presiding Officer, and Councillors of the Tobago House of Assembly
classes.disposition_reason: The Presiding Officer and the Chief Secretary are elected by the Assemblymen, and the four Councillors are appointed on the advice of the Chief Secretary (three) and the Minority Leader (one) (THA Act ss.5 and 7-9); none is chosen by a public vote.

classes.name: Local government elections of councillors
classes.name_en: Municipal corporation councillors (county and municipal councils before 1992)
classes.finest_note: The Commission's 2023 report gives votes by polling station in every electoral district; reports for earlier local elections are not posted, and its Appendix VIII gives only national totals back to 1968.
classes.note: One councillor per electoral district by first past the post (Municipal Corporations Act s.11(3)) in the 14 city, borough, and regional corporations of Trinidad; Tobago has had no local councils since the Tobago House of Assembly replaced its county council in 1980. Councillors served three-year terms under the Act as revised to 2016 (s.11(4)), but elections have often been postponed by Act of Parliament.

cadence.locator: Municipal Corporations Act s.11(4): "The term of office of Councillors shall be three years"; s.11(4A) election within three months of the expiry of the term
cadence.administered_by: Elections and Boundaries Commission, through returning officers it appoints for each electoral district

classes.name: Aldermen allocated to parties from the councillor vote
classes.disposition_reason: Since Act No. 13 of 2013 the Commission allocates each corporation's four aldermen to parties in proportion to their votes in that corporation's councillor elections; there is no separate ballot, and the allocation is derived from results the local_councils class already holds (2023 report, Table 3). Before 2013 aldermen were chosen by the councillors.

classes.name: Mayors, chairmen, and their deputies
classes.disposition_reason: The Mayor (Chairman of a regional corporation) and deputy are elected from among the aldermen and councillors at a council meeting (Municipal Corporations Act s.14); no public vote is held.
